claims.claim: Myosotis is presented as a provisional field-operated AI architecture with device-bounded execution and explicit non-production framing.
limitations: Public summary only; requirements may change while source RFCs remain Draft.

claims.claim: Field environments motivate local authority because connectivity, network trust, sensitive data proximity, and action consequences differ from cloud-first assumptions.
limitations: This is design context, not deployment or reliability evidence.

claims.claim: The design places final execution decisions at the device while allowing central systems to coordinate bounded discovery and routing.
limitations: This describes intended authority boundaries, not a universal production guarantee.

claims.claim: The public safety model uses scoped capabilities, provenance, local enforcement, consent, audit, and fail-closed behavior to bound risk.
limitations: Risk is bounded by design constraints; it is not claimed to be eliminated.

claims.claim: Healthcare-first and other regulated field scenarios inform the design constraints without implying clinical or regulatory validation.
limitations: Examples are non-clinical and do not represent production patient-data handling.

claims.claim: A protocol v0.1 schema/fixture profile and an Android-first deterministic reference-runtime slice exist at the reviewed canonical revision.
limitations: Evidence is limited to the reviewed conformance/runtime slice; no production, performance, regulatory, or clinical claim follows.

claims.claim: The public site is a non-normative review surface and does not create protocol or SDK requirements.
limitations: Canonical requirements remain governed outside the public publication surface.

claims.claim: The design summary is a limited public projection of the RFC set and intentionally avoids production, performance, and efficacy claims.
limitations: Requirements may change while represented RFCs remain Draft.

claims.claim: Myosotis is designed as a security-bounded mobile execution architecture with local policy, explicit invocation, attributable audit, and human consent.
limitations: Architecture intent is not deployment evidence.

claims.claim: The design prioritizes bounded tools, operator clarity, explicit trust boundaries, and containment over unconstrained autonomy.
limitations: These are design principles, not measured safety outcomes.

claims.claim: The architecture separates coordination functions from device-side policy, consent, audit, and execution authority.
limitations: The summary intentionally omits implementation-sensitive detail.

claims.claim: Agent requests and remote authorization metadata do not override device-local policy or create implicit execution authority.
limitations: Specific authorization mechanisms remain governed by the canonical RFCs.

claims.claim: Consent is modeled as a bounded security control and distributed outcomes must remain legible rather than collapsing into ambiguous aggregate success.
limitations: No human-factors or clinical usability outcome is claimed.

claims.claim: Failure handling is designed to fail closed on invalid authority and preserve bounded behavior under degraded conditions.
limitations: This is intended failure behavior, not an availability or reliability guarantee.

claims.claim: The public design summary remains provisional and is not a claim of production validation.
limitations: Public maturity wording is deliberately conservative.

claims.claim: The public summary maps its subject areas to RFC-001 through RFC-014, whose represented statuses are recorded in the provenance manifest.
limitations: RFC identifiers and statuses are public metadata only; private RFC text is not exported.

claims.claim: The threat page is a public, non-exhaustive projection of canonical threat and security-boundary work.
limitations: Exploit-sensitive detail and private analysis are intentionally omitted.

claims.claim: Agents, devices, tools, and coordination systems are treated as untrusted by default, with device-local policy preserving the final execution boundary.
limitations: This is a design invariant, not proof that all implementations satisfy it.

claims.claim: The public threat model includes cross-device escalation, registry poisoning, policy overreach, hidden execution scope, and tool-supply-chain failure classes.
limitations: Threat enumeration is intentionally summarized and is not exhaustive.

claims.claim: The design combines signed artifacts, device-side enforcement, identity, consent, audit, and fail-closed rules to contain identified threat classes.
limitations: Mitigations reduce or contain risk by design; they do not eliminate risk.

claims.claim: Federation must not create remote authority, implicit trust, hidden scope, silent degradation, or mutable unreviewed trust surfaces.
limitations: These are governing constraints subject to canonical RFC evolution.

claims.claim: The threat summary identifies the public RFC metadata that principally informs the page without exposing private RFC text.
limitations: Only identifiers/status are published; detailed analysis remains outside this public projection.
